_comment: Default principle grouping for any planned deslop pass (readings applied to slices). Every per-principle file under references/<category>/ must appear in exactly one lens; scripts/swarm_lenses.py --check enforces that and refuses to emit prompts otherwise. Grouping logic: a lens is a single reading stance — the principles in it are the ones whose findings a reader must weigh against each other (boundary ownership vs boundary parsing vs shape vs legibility). Related principles deliberately live together so a swarmed pass does not report the same smell twice under two names.

stage_protocols.pass-planning.md: before a pass that must cover the library, or after one that missed something
stage_protocols.aggregating-findings.md: the moment more than one reading has reported
stage_protocols.consolidating-and-triage.md: after aggregation, before anything is reported or filed
stage_protocols.reporting-results.md: immediately before reporting to the person who asked
stage_protocols.measuring.md: any pass that will claim a number
stage_protocols.campaign-mode.md: a whole-codebase campaign with a target
stage_protocols.loop-until-dry.md: a thorough pass that must iterate to dry
stage_protocols.extending-the-library.md: adding a principle to the library

situational.case-study-simplification-agent-fleet.md: a worked KISS example, read on request
situational.further-reading.md: bibliography and attribution, not needed mid-audit

boundaries.stance: Where does this code belong, and does each part hold one concern? Judge seams, ownership and cohesion — not function size.

duplication.stance: What knowledge exists more than once, and where is its single owner? Read duplication.md as well — the sweep primitives live there.

coupling.stance: What does each unit know about its neighbours, and what does it construct or reach through that it should have been handed?

parsing.stance: Where does an external value enter, and which single component turns it into a decision? Follow each input from the edge to every place that re-interprets it.

shape.stance: How big and how tangled is each unit's control flow? Depth, conditional chains, parameter lists, nesting — the measurable shape of the code.

legibility.stance: Can a competent stranger read this without the author present? Naming, comment discipline, surprise, elegance, and code that copes where it should decide.

guarantees.stance: What does this code promise, who claims the promise, and what happens when it is broken? State, lifetime, cancellation, privilege, and telling the truth when it fails.

data-layer.stance: If there is a database: what does the schema promise, where is an invariant only in application code, and what access path does each query actually have?
data-layer.skip_when: the target has no schema, migration, ORM model or SQL — say so in the report rather than inventing findings
